components.name: Ladder Steps
components.description: The numbered weekly sequence in the About section.
components.html:
How the ladder works

  1. A pod of four. Each league night you play in a pod with three other players.
  2. Three doubles matches. You partner with each of the other three once.
  3. Ratings update weekly. Elo keeps pods close to your level, and beating someone rated above you moves you the most.
components.css: .ds-ladder { background: #faf7f2; border: 1px solid #ece8e1; border-radius: 20px; padding: 2.25rem 2.5rem; max-width: 560px; } .ds-ladder-title { font-family: 'DM Serif Display', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 1.3rem; color: #1c1c1c; margin: 0 0 1.25rem; } .ds-steps { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 0; counter-reset: ladder; } .ds-steps li { counter-increment: ladder; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 2.5rem 1fr; column-gap: 1rem; padding: 1rem 0; border-top: 1px solid #e2ddd5; font-family: 'DM Sans', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.95rem; line-height: 1.6; color: #6b6b6b; } .ds-steps li:last-child { padding-bottom: 0; } .ds-steps li::before { content: counter(ladder); grid-row: span 2; font-family: 'DM Serif Display', Georgia, serif; font-size: 2rem; line-height: 1; color: #1a7a5c; } .ds-steps strong { display: block; color: #1c1c1c; font-weight: 600; margin-bottom: 0.15rem; }

narrative.overview:
The site reads like the board by the front desk of a club that is run well: warm paper, one confident green, a serif headline pinned at the top, and below it the facts a player came for, set out plainly and kept current. The credibility comes from being organized, not from looking expensive. A visitor comparing this league with the corporate ones should come away thinking "these people have their act together" and never "this is a sales funnel".

Density is relaxed on the homepage and closer to reading density on the inner pages. Sections alternate cream and white like sheets on a board, each opening with a small pill tag and a centred serif heading. Ornament is kept to near nothing: three faint radial washes behind the hero, numerals and ruled lines where content is a sequence or a listing, and a small lift on the buttons. Information such as the schedule table, the League Info list and the callouts is where the care shows.

What it must never become: a corporate league's SaaS page (glossy gradients, stock photos of smiling players, dark promo banners), an aggressive sports brand (black-and-neon, italic condensed type, energy-drink intensity), or a generic startup template (purple gradients, icon-card grids for everything, glass).
keyCharacteristics: Warm cream paper, never stark white as the page ground.
One accent, court green, carries every action and link.
Amber is the reserved "act today" signal, not decoration.
DM Serif Display headings over DM Sans text, both self-hosted.
Soft, rounded, approachable forms: pill buttons and tags, 20px cards.
Facts first: tables, labelled lists and callouts do the persuading.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Court green is the only interactive colour. A link, button or focus ring in any other hue is a bug.

rules.name: The Amber Means Today Rule
rules.body: Amber text marks what a visitor can act on today. Adding it for emphasis or decoration spends the one signal that tells a player registration is open.

rules.name: The 404 Copy Rule
rules.body: 404.html carries its own copy of the palette, which must match :root in css/style.css token for token. The build fails if they drift.

rules.name: The One Weight Serif Rule
rules.body: DM Serif Display ships at weight 400 only. Never bold it: the browser will fake a bold that no font file backs.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Every heading, button and table label is in sentence case ("Learn more", "Registration opens"). The one exception is the homepage h1, "People Over Profits. Pickleball For Everyone.", which is a wordmark and stays in title case by the owner's decision.

rules.name: The Pinned Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces rest flat. Shadows are for the one panel that holds the schedule and for the primary button, never for decoration or for a hover on something that is not clickable.

dos: Do ground every page in cream (cream) and alternate white bands for section rhythm.
Do open each section with a pill tag and a centred DM Serif heading.
Do keep court green as the only colour for links, buttons and focus.
Do reserve amber text (amber-dark) for what a visitor can act on today.
Do keep text at 4.5:1 or better. The build computes the contrast of the key pairs, so a new pairing needs a check too.
Do keep every link underlined unless it is a button or nav item, and add any new exception to the named list.
Do keep all assets self-hosted and the styles in the hashed stylesheet. The CSP forbids inline styles and third-party hosts.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion: transitions and animations become instant, and smooth scrolling turns off.
donts: Don't use glossy gradients, stock photography, or dark promo banners. That is the corporate-league look this site exists to contrast with.
Don't use black-and-neon palettes, italic condensed type or high-energy sports styling.
Don't use purple gradients, glassmorphism, or icon-card grids as a default layout move.
Don't add photos, testimonials or quotes the league does not have.
Don't bold DM Serif Display or add a second display face.
Don't use amber (#e8860c) for text, or ink-faint on cream.
Don't add sharp corners or hard drop shadows. Forms stay soft and rounded.
